title: Runlet mapper and policy fabrication for safe admin automation
creator: Maya R. Chen
description: Deliver a lightweight 'runlet mapper' that turns curated runbook fragments into executable, policy-wrapped tasks. The goal is an opinionated translation layer that enforces safety constraints (time limits, permission checks, dry-run mode) and emits structured telemetry so support tooling can automatically chain, retry, or escalate steps. This is intended to reduce oncall cognitive load for common maintenance flows while keeping full operator control for complex remediation.
tasks: Design runlet manifest schema (inputs, outputs, invariants, permissions)
Prototype mapper that compiles runlet manifest to task spec (YAML/JSON) with guard hooks
Implement permission-check plugin and KMS-signed permit tokens
Add idempotency keys and step-level retry/backoff semantics
Integrate dry-run mode that simulates side-effects and records alternative telemetry
Wire telemetry: step-level success/failure, latency, side-effect-intent, and rollup counts
Create a safety sandbox and CI job to run canonical runlets against simulator
Author migration script for converting 20 high-frequency manual runbooks into runlets
acceptance_criteria: Runlet manifest schema reviewed and approved by Security and SRE
Mapper compiles 90% of chosen runbook fragments without manual edits
Permission checks enforced: actions requiring elevated scope fail without signed permit
Idempotency prevents duplicate side-effects within 10 minute window for common steps
Dry-run produces full deterministic plan and no external side-effects
Telemetry surfaces step-level failure reasons and is visible in Console runbooks dashboard
2 post-migration runlets executed by oncall without manual rollbacks in staging
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff with SRE and Security; established threat model and minimum guardrails
2025-01-18: First draft of manifest schema posted to Confluence (link in links)
2025-01-22: Prototype mapper compiles simple 'rotate-ssl-cert' runbook fragment to task spec
2025-01-29: Permission-check approach chosen: short-lived KMS-signed permits with auditable token IDs
2025-02-02: Dry-run simulation implemented; discovered two non-deterministic shell steps in legacy runbook
2025-02-04: Held review with support team; agreed to convert 6 highest-frequency runbooks in phase 1
review_feedback: Security: require permit tokens to include a purpose field and TTL to limit replay risk
SRE: add circuit-breaker hook for steps that touch stateful clusters (e.g., node drains)
Support lead: prefer readable human-friendly plan output for dry-run to reduce cognitive load
Design: add an optional annotated example in Console for each runlet to show before/after
notes: Trade-offs considered: embedding full scripting support vs. constrained step primitives. Chosen path is constrained primitives + escape hatch via reviewed permit tokens to reduce blast radius.
Planned rollout: feature-flagged on staging -> limited oncall beta -> org-wide release. Each runlet migration will include a 48h watch window.
Failure modes: mapper could mis-classify a step's side-effects. Mitigation: automated simulation tests and a pre-flight dry-run that must be acknowledged.
Telemetry plan: emit event per runlet step with tags {runlet_id, step_id, side_effect_intent, permit_present, dry_run}. Charting in Console and alerts for unexpected error spikes.
Estimated effort split: 3 dev sprints to prototype + 1 sprint for hardening + 1 sprint for migration tooling. Cross-team reviewers: SRE, Security, Support, Design.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): manifest schema + mapper for read-only and benign operations
Phase 2 (safety): implement permits, idempotency, dry-run and telemetry hooks
Phase 3 (migration): convert and test top-6 runbooks in staging, collect feedback
Phase 4 (scale): create migration scripts, CI simulators, promote to beta and GA
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental production changes from buggy mapping. Mitigation: default to dry-run and require signed permit for mutating runlets.
Risk: insufficient telemetry granularity for debugging. Mitigation: early integration with Console runbook dashboard and retained traces for 7 days
Risk: oncall confusion over runlet behavior. Mitigation: provide clear human-readable plan output and 'explain' endpoint for each runlet
